title: Smoothed singular-series sum and the ratio profile
statement: Let f and ρ be as in problem.md and put ρ(1)=1. For each integer h≥1 define W_f(h)=∏_p(1−2/p²)[1+ρ(p^{max{2−v_p(h),0}})/(p^{max{2−v_p(h),0}}(p²−2))], where products are over primes and v_p(h) is the exponent of p in h. Let D_f(s)=Σ_{h≥1}W_f(h)h^(−s), initially for Re(s)>1 and then by meromorphic continuation. Define R_f=Res_{s=1}D_f(s), B_f=lim_{s→1}[D_f(s)−R_f/(s−1)]−3R_f/2, K_f=−(16/3)Res_{s=−1/2}D_f(s), and c=ζ(2)^(−1), with ζ the Riemann zeta function. For real H≥1 put Θ_f(H)=Σ_{1≤h≤H}W_f(h)(H−h)²/h and F_f(H)=R_f log H+B_f+c/H−Θ_f(H)/H². There is C(f)>0 such that, uniformly for all real H≥1, |Θ_f(H)−[R_fH²log H+B_fH²+cH−K_fH^(1/2)]|≤C(f)H^(3/8), and consequently |F_f(H)−K_fH^(−3/2)|≤C(f)H^(−13/8). Moreover, uniformly for real x≥2 and 2≤Z≤Y≤x, 2∫_Z^Y Σ_{1≤h≤x/t}(x−ht)W_f(h)dt=Z²Θ_f(x/Z)−Y²Θ_f(x/Y).
cites: R. C. Vaughan, A variance for k-free numbers in arithmetic progressions (2005), Lemma 2.18, for the Mellin-transform framework; https://doi.org/10.1112/S0024611505015352.
H. L. Montgomery and R. C. Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory I: Classical Theory (2007), Corollary 10.4, the zeta functional equation; https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511618314.
risk: The Mellin kernel is 2/[s(s+1)(s+2)] applied to D_f(s+1). The residue at s=−1 has a negative kernel residue, producing +cH. A sign error there prevents diagonal cancellation. The contour shift to Re(s)=−13/8 must include an explicit integrable vertical bound.
